messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: leadership@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly Lodestar Signal — wins, risks, asks (May 24)

Team — quick weekly pulse ahead of QBR prep. High-level bullets first, then asks.

Wins:
- Zephyr pilot: latency SLO met at 95th percentile (12ms over target) across 3k calls/day. Early feedback positive; Sarah Gold confirmed integration tests passed.
- Dedicate pool autoscale: rolled out Thursday with no infra incidents; avg throughput up 18%.

Risks/Chokepoints:
- Capacity heat: projected peak for mid-June could exceed Dedicated capacity by ~22% if Zephyr expands to full production. See attached capacity-heatmap.csv.
- QBR deck still has a slide gap on revenue impact (we have cost/perf but need $ impact by Friday).

Asks / Next steps:
1) Marcus — can you provide a 1-slide revenue delta (token-cost to revenue conversion) by Thu EOD? Attach to the deck.
2) Karthik — recommend we hold the small model rollout to the EU pool until autoscale policy is tuned. Need your call by EOD Wed.
3) Laura — can you add a 90s exec note to slide 2 that summarizes the operational ask for capacity and net impact?

Attachments: lodestar-ops-snapshot.pdf, qbr-deck-v1.pptx, capacity-heatmap.csv

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Head of Operations | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Thanks Ava — solid signal. Two quick clarifications: 

- Marcus: can you make the revenue delta slide include both ARR-runrate and 12-month projected delta (high/medium/low scenarios)? Execs will want the tail-risk numbers.
- On Zephyr: Sarah asked if we can guarantee no PII persists in logs for the pilot expansion; Marcus or Marissa can you confirm current redaction/retention settings? If not, we need an evidence note for procurement.

Also copying procurement (contracts@procureco.com) — we may need a rapid amendment if Zephyr moves to extended pilot.

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 13:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly Lodestar Signal — wins, risks, asks (May 24)

Agree with the conservative approach on EU rollout. Quick notes: 
- The autoscale policy is reducing tail latency but we see a split in seq-length distributions between EU test traffic and US production; that creates a risk of KV-cache churn that could spike GPU memory usage.
- Proposed mitigation: delay small-model EU rollout by one sprint and deploy an adjusted kernel selection that caps prefetch concurrency. That gives SRE 10 business days to verify memory behavior under synthetic peak.

If leadership wants the rollout earlier, we can do a partial canary limited to 10% of EU traffic, but I recommend the delay.

Karthik
VP, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
